aliases: An Xi Gan De Tie Guan Yin
processing: Made as Anxi Tie Guan Yin generally is: partial oxidation, repeated rolling into pellets and drying. No separate township method is recorded.
harvest_season: Spring and autumn, like all Anxi Tie Guan Yin; the autumn season draws a lively market in Gande.
appearance_dry: Tight green pellets, as is typical of Anxi Tie Guan Yin in the light style.
appearance_liquor: Pale yellow-green and clear, as with light Anxi Tie Guan Yin.
appearance_wet: Whole leaves unfurl, as with other Tie Guan Yin.
taste_profile: Local saying singles out Gande for fragrance, so expect a tea led by aroma, with the orchid-like florals typical of Tie Guan Yin. Reliable notes specific to the town are scarce.

brewing.notes: Treat it as a light Tie Guan Yin: rinse quickly, keep water just off the boil and use a porcelain gaiwan to show the aroma.

vintage_note: Sold by season and year like other Anxi Tie Guan Yin, usually the spring or autumn of the current year. Drink the light style within about a year and keep it sealed. The town name on the pack is a claim of origin, and ask the seller which village and which harvest it came from.
description:
Gande is a mountain township in Inner Anxi, the higher western part of the county, and Tie Guan Yin labelled with its name is a claim about place, not a separate type of tea. Its reputation comes through a local saying that gives each area a virtue: Gande fragrance, Xianghua flavour, Xiping charm.

The processing is standard for Anxi, so the case for Gande rests on terrain. Inner Anxi is mountainous and misty, with acidic red soil, and Gande is counted among the county's main Tie Guan Yin towns.

Expect the usual pattern of light Tie Guan Yin, with florals and a creamy texture, and pay attention to how far the aroma carries, since that is the local boast. Very hot water and short steeps work best.

The label is hard to verify from outside, and the saying about fragrance is folklore, not a standard. Try it next to a Xiping or Xianghua tea of the same season to decide whether the difference is real for you.
history: Gande's tea is documented mainly through its place in the wider Anxi trade, and little has been written about the town's own history. It has been promoted under the title of China's leading Tie Guan Yin town. A 2017 press report from the autumn season described its tea market as crowded enough to cause traffic jams.
